title: Dhaka Slum Fires
dek: How catastrophic 'accidental' fires bypass constitutional eviction protections to clear high-value urban transit corridors in Dhaka.
summary: A forensic spatial overlay investigation tracing two decades of catastrophic informal settlement fires along high-value commercial and road transit corridors in Dhaka, showing how fire functions as a bypass for constitutional shelter rights.
key_findings: Dhaka's rapid transport corridor expansion correlates directly with catastrophic fires in adjacent informal settlements, bypassing court-mandated eviction protections.
A 20-year multi-site baseline reveals that fires at Korail, Chalantika, Sattola, and Kalshi slums cleared valuable state-owned land for high-end flat projects, ICT villages, and flyover ramps.
At Kalshi slum, land value appreciation spiked +250% following the Tk 1,012 crore flyover opening, immediately preceding the May 2026 fire that cleared 1,200 structures.
